title: Another autoimmune CAR-T death; Treasury zeroes in on China deals
content: An article from News roundup Another autoimmune CAR-T death; Treasury zeroes in on China deals A patient who received Bristol Myers’ zola-cel died 44 days later. Elsewhere, Gilead paid nearly $1.3 billion for a potential threat to J&J’s newly approved psoriasis pill. Published Oct. 26, 2026 Ben Fidler Lead Editor Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Getty Images Today, a brief rundown of news involving Bristol Myers Squibb and the U.S. Department of the Treasury, as well as updates from Gilead Sciences and Zymeworks that you may have missed. A trial participant who received an experimental autoimmune cell therapy from Bristol Myers Squibb died 44 days later, the company said Friday. Following an infusion with “zola-cel” in a multiple sclerosis study, the trial participant experienced what Bristol Myers described as “late onset ... motor symptoms” that couldn’t be quelled by steroids and other drugs. The volunteer later developed septic pneumonia and died shortly afterward. Bristol Myers said no other deaths have been observed in that study or any other autoimmune disease trial of zola-cel. It also touted findings suggesting the therapy’s potential to “reset” the immune system in people with MS. Still, the company as well as Novartis previously paused multiple autoimmune cell therapy studies due to safety concerns. The Treasury is seeking public comments before finalizing the rules. Gilead Sciences on Thursday agreed to pay nearly $1.3 billion in cash to acquire an experimental immune disease drug from Shanghai, China-based PepStar Therapeutics. Zymeworks and Roche will collaborate on a Phase 1a study, with the Swiss pharmaceutical giant taking over global development afterward. title: AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 15, 2026 AstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 Billion Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff AstraZeneca will pay insitro $40 million upfront to apply AI to target discovery in MASH and cardiomyopathies, with no candidates named yet. Advertisement AstraZeneca has signed a drug discovery collaboration and licensing agreement with insitro to apply artificial intelligence (AI) to target identification and therapeutic design in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and cardiomyopathies, the companies announced Oct. 15.1,2 Insitro will receive $40 million upfront and is eligible for up to approximately $1.46 billion in milestones.1,2Sharon Barr, executive vice president and head of BioPharmaceuticals research and development at AstraZeneca, tied the agreement to target selection: “We know that disease biology is incredibly complex, and one of the most critical decisions in R&D is selecting the right target. This strategic collaboration underscores our commitment to maximizing the potential of cutting-edge AI to tackle the root cause of disease. Partnering with insitro, we will use advanced AI to identify the biological drivers of disease to support the rapid discovery of high-quality novel targets, advancing our ambition to deliver the next generation of medicines to patients faster.”1“MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights.”What are AstraZeneca and insitro agreeing to do?Insitro will use its Virtual Human platform to identify causal disease biology in both indications and advance AstraZeneca-nominated targets from discovery to development candidate.1,2 The platform combines large-scale human and cellular data with AI-enabled target identification and medicine design.1AstraZeneca will take the clinical development and regulatory work and holds exclusive worldwide rights to the selected programs; insitro’s release adds that AstraZeneca will also lead commercialization.1,2Beyond the upfront payment, insitro is eligible for single-digit royalties on global sales.1,2 The two releases describe the milestones slightly differently: AstraZeneca cites development and commercial milestones, while insitro includes discovery milestones.1,2The upfront payment represents less than 3% of the combined headline value, and neither company disclosed the number of targets, program timelines or payment schedule.Why are MASH and cardiomyopathies difficult to treat?Insitro’s release says each disease is defined by heterogeneity, with a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs, which has complicated treatment.2 (()=>{var l=(n,t)=>{let i=async()=>{await(await n())()},e=typeof t.value=="object"?t.value:void 0,s={timeout:e==null?void 0:e.timeout};"requestIdleCallback"in window?window.requestIdleCallback(i,s):setTimeout(i,s.timeout||200)};(self.Astro||(self.Astro={})).idle=l;window.dispatchEvent(new Event("astro:idle"));})(); Daphne Koller, Ph.D., founder and CEO of insitro, said: “MASH and cardiomyopathies are prevalent, underdiagnosed diseases where high-content data holds immense potential for uncovering disease drivers. By applying AI to these complex datasets, we can unlock greater discovery power and reveal novel genetic insights. Our platform simultaneously deconvolutes disease biology and identifies causal drivers of disease pathologies. Partnering with AstraZeneca allows us to pair our deep biological precision with their pharmaceutical expertise and scale with potential for accelerated advancement of novel programs through development and to patients.”2In MASH, the treatment landscape has changed recently. The FDA approved resmetirom (Rezdiffra) in March 2024 under its accelerated approval pathway for adults with noncirrhotic disease and moderate to advanced liver scarring, to be used with diet and exercise. The agency, which at the time referred to the condition as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis, said patients had previously lacked a medication that directly addressed their liver damage, and cited an estimate of 6 million to 8 million U.S. patients at that disease stage.3The cardiomyopathy picture is less defined in the releases, which do not specify which forms are in scope. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, the most common inherited cardiovascular disorder, is estimated to affect 1 in 500 people, and a published review notes that existing studies may have underestimated its prevalence.4 That offers one illustration of the underdiagnosis Koller describes, though it should not be read as the collaboration’s target population.How does the collaboration fit each company’s portfolio?AstraZeneca describes cardiovascular, renal and metabolism as one of its main disease areas and a key growth driver, with an emphasis on the links among the heart, kidneys, liver and pancreas.1 A program spanning a liver disease and heart muscle diseases fits within that framing.Insitro says it has built a multimodal corpus of human and cellular data since 2018 and is advancing nine programs, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.2 The company reports more than $750 million in capital and existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead.2 The release does not say how its internal liver programs relate to targets AstraZeneca will nominate.What remains unknown about the collaboration?No candidate, efficacy data or safety data accompany the announcement, and the collaboration sits at the discovery stage. Targets identified through AI-driven analysis of human data will still need validation through preclinical work and clinical trials, where heterogeneity of disease could also affect trial design. Milestone and royalty figures are potential payments contingent on progress that neither company has timed publicly. content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 28, 2026 Roundup: Astellas Licenses IL-12 Fusion Protein From Audax in Deal Worth Up to $1.34 Billion, EVERSANA Acquires Health Economics Firm Estima Scientific Author(s)Pharmaceutical Executive Editorial Staff Astellas gains an option on Audax’s IL-12 antibody-cytokine fusion DAX-044, while EVERSANA acquires London-based health economics firm Estima Scientific. Advertisement Two transactions announced this week sit at opposite ends of the biopharma value chain: access to an early-stage immuno-oncology program, and the technology used to show payers what a product is worth. Astellas Pharma Inc. secured an exclusive option on an investigational cancer therapy from Audax Biosciences Pty Ltd, in a deal valued at up to US$1.34 billion excluding royalties.1 EVERSANA, a commercial services provider to the biopharmaceutical industry, acquired Estima Scientific, a London-based health economics and outcomes research (HEOR) technology company, for undisclosed terms.2Key FactsAstellas–Audax: option and license for DAX-044DAX-044: IL-12 antibody-cytokine fusionValue: up to US$1.34B, excluding royaltiesPhase 1 expected to begin in 2027EVERSANA acquires London-based Estima ScientificEstima: generative AI tools for HEOREVERSANA deal terms: not disclosedAstellas Gains Option on Audax’s IL-12 Antibody-Cytokine FusionAstellas and Audax, an Australian biotechnology company, entered an exclusive option and license agreement for DAX-044, an investigational, immune-targeted interleukin-12 (IL-12) antibody-cytokine fusion for immuno-oncology.1 “By combining Audax’s innovative science with Astellas’ development, manufacturing and commercialization expertise, we hope to advance a potential new treatment option for patients with solid tumors, including cancers where effective immune stimulation remains an important therapeutic challenge,” says Takahiko Iwaya, chief strategy officer at Astellas.If Astellas exercises the option, it would receive a worldwide license to develop, manufacture and commercialize DAX-044 and assume sole responsibility for those activities. Audax has the option to co-fund and co-promote the drug in Australia and New Zealand. Exercise is subject to customary conditions, including antitrust clearances.1 Total potential value reaches up to US$1.34 billion, excluding royalties. Audax would receive US$285 million through an upfront payment and a potential option exercise payment, plus up to US$1.05 billion in development and commercial milestones and tiered double-digit royalties on worldwide net sales if the drug is approved.1 Audax will fund and continue development into a Phase 1 study expected to begin in 2027.1Why has IL-12 been difficult to develop as a cancer therapy?DAX-044 uses the AVIKINE antibody-cytokine platform and is designed to concentrate IL-12’s immune-activating activity in the tumor microenvironment while limiting the systemic toxicity that has historically constrained IL-12-based therapy.1 That constraint is documented. Patrik Jonsson will retire from Eli Lilly at the end of 2026, completing a 36-year run at the Indianapolis-based drugmaker. content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 注册审批 科伦博泰B7-H3 ADC药物SKB500联合PD-1/VEGF双抗获批临床，经治SCLC患者有望解锁更优治疗方案 科伦博泰B7-H3 ADC药物SKB500联合PD-1/VEGF双抗获批临床，经治SCLC患者有望解锁更优治疗方案 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 19小时前 1108 科伦博泰 B7-H3 ADC药物 临床试验 小细胞肺癌 SKB500 SKB118 10月26日，CDE官网显示，科伦博泰自主研发的B7-H3 ADC药物SKB500联合PD-1/VEGF双抗SKB118，用于小细胞肺癌（SCLC）患者的Ⅱ期临床试验申请获批。图源：CDE官网此次联用将B7-H3 ADC与同时靶向PD-1、VEGF通路的双抗相结合，进一步探索ADC联合免疫治疗在SCLC中的应用潜力。一、SKB500Ⅰ期数据公布，ORR最高达75%SKB500是一款科伦博泰自主研发的B7-H3 ADC，采用高亲和力、高亲水性及内吞作用更强的抗体，并通过可裂解的亲水性AAA连接子连接载荷，药物抗体比（DAR）约为8。2026年ESMO大会上，科伦博泰公布了SKB500治疗广泛期小细胞肺癌（ES-SCLC）的Ⅰ期研究数据。扩展队列共纳入61例既往接受过系统治疗的患者，所有患者均接受过含铂治疗，其中85.2%接受过PD-(L)1抑制剂治疗。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库截至2026年9月16日，12 mg/kg组和16 mg/kg组的中位随访时间分别为9.3个月和8.3个月，关键数据如下：客观缓解率（ORR）：分别为75.0%和66.7%。中位无进展生存期（mPFS）：分别为8.1个月和5.6个月。中位总生存期（mOS）：分别为14.0个月和10.6个月。安全性：两组≥3级治疗相关不良事件（TRAE）发生率分别为52.5%和66.7%，常见不良事件包括血液学毒性和胃肠道毒性，未报告治疗相关死亡。上述结果来自早期临床研究，后续仍需进一步验证。二、联合PD-1/VEGF双抗，拓展ADC联用策略SKB118（CR-001）由科伦博泰与Crescent联合开发，可同时靶向PD-1和VEGF通路，目前已在中国和美国启动单药Ⅰ期临床试验。此前，科伦博泰已推进SKB118与TROP2 ADC芦康沙妥珠单抗（sac-TMT）的联合开发。此次SKB500与SKB118的联用临床申请获批，进一步拓展了公司在ADC与双抗联合治疗领域的布局。同类联合方案也在持续探索。今年WCLC期间，BNT324/DB-1311联合PD-L1/VEGF双抗Pumitamig治疗肺癌的Ⅰb/Ⅱ期研究公布数据。在71例SCLC患者中，ORR为70.4%；按治疗线数划分，一线、二线及三线及以上患者的ORR分别为92.3%、77.3%和52.4%。这一研究为ADC联合PD-(L)1/VEGF双抗治疗SCLC提供了进一步的临床探索依据，但不同研究的患者人群和设计存在差异，相关数据不宜直接比较。三、多款创新药推进临床，研发管线持续拓展科伦博泰持续推进创新药研发。截至目前，科伦博泰已有3款1类新药获批上市，包括注射用芦康沙妥珠单抗、塔戈利单抗注射液和注射用博度曲妥珠单抗。图源：摩熵医药-中国药品审评数据库此外，科伦药业（含子公司）有超30款1类新药处于获批IND及以上阶段，涉及抗肿瘤药物、神经系统药物、系统用抗感染药物等疾病领域。 content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 注册审批 拜耳1类新药阿舒克森片国内获批上市！非心源性缺血性卒中二级预防迎来FXIa抑制剂全新解决方案 拜耳1类新药阿舒克森片国内获批上市！非心源性缺血性卒中二级预防迎来FXIa抑制剂全新解决方案 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 20小时前 890 拜耳 FXIa抑制剂 阿舒克森片 优先审评 获批上市 缺血性卒中 10月26日，摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库显示，拜耳申报的FXIa抑制剂阿舒克森片（Asundexian）通过优先审评程序获批上市，用于降低缺血性卒中或高风险短暂性脑缺血发作（TIA）后成人患者的卒中风险，不包括心源性栓塞型卒中患者。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库Asundexian是一款靶向凝血因子XI活化形式（FXIa）的口服抑制剂，旨在减少病理性血栓形成。本次获批主要基于全球Ⅲ期OCEANIC-STROKE研究结果。一、全球Ⅲ期研究：缺血性卒中风险降低26%OCEANIC-STROKE是一项多中心、随机、双盲、安慰剂对照的全球Ⅲ期研究，共纳入12327名受试者，评估Asundexian联合抗血小板治疗在非心源性缺血性卒中或高风险TIA后患者中的疗效与安全性。摩熵医药数据库显示，该药于2026年4月30日首次申报上市获受理。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2026年2月，拜耳公布该研究数据。结果显示，与安慰剂联合抗血小板治疗相比，Asundexian联合抗血小板治疗使患者缺血性卒中发生风险显著降低26%（csHR=0.74，95% CI：0.65–0.84，p＜0.0001）。在安全性方面，Asundexian组与安慰剂组的国际血栓与止血学会（ISTH）定义的大出血发生率分别为1.9%和1.7%，组间未见显著差异（HR=1.10，95% CI：0.85–1.44）。二、多项次要终点也显示获益研究的次要终点结果显示，与安慰剂相比，Asundexian组任何类型卒中（包括缺血性和出血性卒中）的发生风险降低26%，发生率分别为6.6%和8.8%（csHR=0.74，95% CI：0.65–0.84，p＜0.0001）。此外，在心血管死亡、心肌梗死或卒中，以及任何原因死亡、心肌梗死或卒中的复合终点方面，Asundexian组也达到相应次要有效性终点。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库研究还纳入了不同病因亚型的缺血性卒中患者。按TOAST标准分类，在所评估的各类亚型中，Asundexian组的缺血性卒中复发发生率均低于安慰剂组。此次中国获批，为缺血性卒中或高风险TIA后患者的卒中风险管理提供了新的治疗选择。随着FXIa抑制剂研发推进，其在降低血栓事件风险与控制出血风险之间的平衡，也成为这一领域的重要关注方向。扩展阅读：1. title: 罗氏divarasib头对头Ⅲ期临床研究数据出炉，KRAS G12C突变NSCLC患者死亡风险直降44%
content: 首页 资讯 摩熵原创 时讯 罗氏divarasib头对头Ⅲ期临床研究数据出炉，KRAS G12C突变NSCLC患者死亡风险直降44% 罗氏divarasib头对头Ⅲ期临床研究数据出炉，KRAS G12C突变NSCLC患者死亡风险直降44% 张鹏 · 新药研发分析师 张 张鹏 新药研发分析师 审核：王正晴 · 药学博士 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 昨天 10:43 2014 ALK7 KRAS G12C 大睿生物医药科技（上海）有限公司 非小细胞肺癌 RO-7435846片 10月25日，在欧洲临床肿瘤学会（ESMO）大会上，罗氏公布了下一代KRAS G12C抑制剂divarasib的Ⅲ期临床研究Krascendo 1最新数据。结果显示，在既往接受过治疗的KRAS G12C突变非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）患者中，与对照组已获批的KRAS G12C抑制剂相比，divarasib将患者死亡风险降低44%，无进展生存期（PFS）和客观缓解率（ORR）也均取得改善。图源：罗氏官网此次研究直接比较了divarasib与安进的Lumakras（sotorasib）、百时美施贵宝（BMS）的Krazati（adagrasib），为其在KRAS G12C突变NSCLC领域的竞争力提供了进一步证据。一、死亡风险降低44%，OS、PFS双双改善Krascendo 1是一项纳入338例患者的Ⅲ期临床研究，旨在评估divarasib在既往接受过治疗的KRAS G12C突变NSCLC患者中的疗效与安全性。今年7月，罗氏首次公布该研究的顶线结果，宣布divarasib在总生存期（OS）和无进展生存期（PFS）方面，较Lumakras和Krazati取得具有临床意义和统计学显著性的改善，但当时尚未披露具体数据。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库10月25日公布的最新分析进一步揭示了这一优势。在生存获益方面，divarasib组中位OS达到17.7个月，对照组为12.0个月，死亡风险降低44%（HR=0.56）。在疾病进展方面，divarasib组中位PFS达到9.8个月，对照组为5.7个月，疾病进展或死亡风险降低42%。在肿瘤缓解方面，divarasib组确认的客观缓解率（ORR）达到58%，对照组为32%。从中位OS、PFS到ORR，divarasib均显示出疗效优势。其中，OS结果尤其受到关注，意味着该药的临床获益不仅体现在延缓疾病进展，也体现在患者生存结局的改善。罗氏首席医学官Levi Garraway表示，这项头对头研究的结果凸显了divarasib为既往接受过治疗的KRAS G12C突变肺癌患者带来新治疗选择的潜力，并进一步支持其同类最佳（best-in-class）的定位。二、疗效之外，安全性数据同步披露除疗效结果外，此次公布的数据还进一步呈现了divarasib的安全性特征。研究显示，divarasib的安全性特征与KRAS G12C抑制剂已知的类效应基本一致，最常见的治疗相关不良事件（TRAE）包括胃肠道毒性和肝毒性。其中，胃肠道不良事件主要表现为腹泻、恶心和呕吐。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库值得关注的是，divarasib组严重腹泻发生率为9%，高于对照组的3%；但因治疗相关不良事件而中断治疗的发生率仅为4.8%，低于对照组的11.7%。此外，研究显示，divarasib在OS和PFS方面的临床获益在各临床相关亚组中保持一致，且不受PD-L1表达水平或KEAP1突变状态影响。整体来看，divarasib在展现疗效优势的同时，也呈现出值得进一步关注的安全性数据。不过，严重腹泻发生率较高这一信号仍需结合更完整的安全性数据进行评估。三、一线治疗布局同步推进除针对既往接受过治疗患者的Krascendo 1研究外，罗氏还在推进divarasib的一线治疗布局。Ⅲ期Krascendo 2研究旨在评估divarasib联合默沙东Keytruda（pembrolizumab）的无化疗方案，对比化疗联合免疫治疗，用于KRAS G12C突变NSCLC一线治疗的疗效与安全性。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库如果后续研究取得积极结果，divarasib有望进一步拓展其在KRAS G12C突变NSCLC治疗中的应用空间。从目前公布的Ⅲ期数据来看，divarasib已在既往接受过治疗的患者中展现出OS、PFS及ORR方面的优势。随着一线治疗研究推进，其后续临床进展值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] 企业官网/官方披露[2] 摩熵医药（原药融云）数据库扩展阅读：1. 罗氏11.6亿美元重金引进大睿生物ALK7 RNAi，同步押注非GLP-1减重与RAS G12V肿瘤双赛道2. 关注全球创新药研发管线、临床试验进展与注册审批动态；重点分析热门靶点、临床价值与管线竞争格局。累计发布研发分析 102+ 篇。 2026/10/26 2791 PD-1 中山康方生物医药有限公司 依沃西单抗 VEGF 胆道癌 10月23日，CDE官网公示，康方生物的依沃西单抗注射液一项新适应症拟纳入优先审评，拟用于联合化疗一线治疗局部晚期或转移性胆道癌。图源：CDE官网此次申报进展与Ⅲ期临床研究HARMONi-GI1取得积极结果有关。2026年8月，康方生物宣布，该研究在预设期中分析中达到总生存期（OS）主要终点，并达到无进展生存期（PFS）和客观缓解率（ORR）的全部关键次要终点。一、胆道癌Ⅲ期研究取得阳性结果依沃西单抗是康方生物自主研发的PD-1/VEGF双特异性抗体，也是全球首创的PD-1/VEGF双特异性肿瘤免疫治疗药物。摩熵医药全球药物研发数据库显示，2024年该品种在中国首次上市。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库本次拟纳入优先审评的新适应症为依沃西单抗联合化疗一线治疗局部晚期或转移性胆道癌。在Ⅲ期临床研究AK112-309/HARMONi-GI1中，研究人员采用随机、双盲、对照、多中心设计，评估依沃西单抗联合化疗与度伐利尤单抗联合化疗一线治疗晚期胆道恶性肿瘤的疗效与安全性。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库2026年8月，康方生物宣布，经独立数据监察委员会（IDMC）评估的预设期中分析显示，HARMONi-GI1研究达到OS主要终点，结果具有统计学显著性；同时达到PFS和ORR的全部关键次要终点。康方生物在新闻稿中表示，度伐利尤单抗联合化疗是国内外指南共同推荐的一线标准治疗方案（SOC）。公司称，HARMONi-GI1是胆道癌领域首个以PD-L1单抗联合化疗为对照、取得OS显著阳性结果的Ⅲ期研究。该研究结果已入选2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）大会突破性摘要（LBA8，主席论坛），康方生物将于大会首次披露具体研究数据。二、依沃西单抗持续拓展适应症目前，依沃西单抗已在中国获批三项适应症，覆盖EGFR-TKI耐药的非鳞状非小细胞肺癌（nsq-NSCLC）、PD-L1阳性非小细胞肺癌一线治疗及鳞状非小细胞肺癌一线治疗。图源：摩熵医药-全球药物研发数据库除国内市场外，依沃西单抗也在推进海外商业化。2022年12月，康方生物将依沃西单抗部分海外权益授权给美国Summit Therapeutics，交易方案包括50亿美元以上的潜在付款及两位数百分比的销售提成。目前，依沃西单抗联合化疗用于第三代EGFR-TKI治疗后进展的EGFR突变非鳞状非小细胞肺癌的美国上市申请正在审评中。此次胆道癌新适应症拟纳入优先审评，意味着依沃西单抗在肺癌之外进一步拓展实体瘤治疗领域。后续研究具体数据及审评进展，值得持续关注。参考来源：[1] CDE官网[2] title: STAT Plus: Tango reports 82% tumor response rate in trial of combo therapy for advanced pancreatic cancer
content: STAT PlusBiotech Tango reports 82% tumor response rate in trial of combo therapy for advanced pancreatic cancer Study presented at ESMO boosts idea that patients benefit more from combining targeted drugs Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Adobe By Adam FeuersteinOct. 23, 2026 Adam Feuerstein, a senior writer and biotech columnist, is the author of Adam’s Biotech Scorecard, a subscriber-only newsletter about the crossroads of drug development, business, Wall Street, and biotechnology. Adam Feuerstein[email protected]Adam Feuerstein is a senior writer and biotech columnist, reporting on the crossroads of drug development, business, Wall Street, and biotechnology. He is also a co-host of the weekly biotech podcast The Readout Loud and author of the newsletter Adam’s Biotech Scorecard. You can reach Adam on Signal at stataf.54. MADRID — The combination of an experimental drug from Tango Therapeutics and Revolution Medicines’ Rasonque led to tumor responses in 82% of patients with a certain type of advanced pancreatic cancer, clinical trial results reported Friday showed. The responses were also durable: 88% of the patients were still alive without tumor progression when assessed at nine months. They still struggle to access it The new data bolster the theory that patients with pancreatic cancer can derive more benefit from combinations of targeted drugs than single drugs. The Tango regimen is also notable for the absence of chemotherapy, long considered a standard treatment for the aggressive cancer. STAT+ Exclusive Story Already have an account? title: Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 19, 2026 Your Questions Answered: Foundayo’s EU Panel Backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s Masked TCE Bet, FDA’s Rare Disease Overhaul, and More Foundayo’s EU backing, Enspryng for TED, Gilead’s masked TCE deal, FDA’s rare disease reset, and Bausch + Lomb’s new interim CEO — explained. Advertisement Lilly’s Foundayo Receives Positive CHMP Opinion for EuropeWhat did the EMA committee recommend?The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use recommended granting marketing authorization in the EU for Foundayo (orforglipron) for two indications: weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, and the treatment of type 2 diabetes in adults whose blood glucose is not adequately controlled. The European Commission makes the final approval decision and typically follows CHMP recommendations within a few weeks.What is Foundayo and why does it matter?Foundayo is Eli Lilly’s oral GLP-1 receptor agonist — a once-daily pill that can be taken at any time of day without food and water restrictions. That last point distinguishes it from other oral GLP-1 therapies currently on the market. The drug received FDA approval for obesity in April 2026 and launched commercially in the United States in the second quarter. Lilly has submitted orforglipron for regulatory review in approximately 40 markets globally.The Stories Covered in this PieceEMA Panel Backs Lilly’s Foundayo for Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes in EuropeFDA Approves Enspryng (Satralizumab) for Thyroid Eye DiseaseAstraZeneca Taps insitro AI for MASH in Deal Worth Up to $1.5 BillionFDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeVir Biotechnology Enters R&D Collaboration with Gilead for Three Novel PRO-XTEN Dual Masked T-Cell EngagersBausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat does this mean competitively?If the European Commission approves Foundayo, it would become the second oral GLP-1 available in the EU for weight management, following Novo Nordisk’s Wegovy pill, which received European approval in July for weight management only. In the type 2 diabetes setting, Foundayo would compete with Novo’s Rybelsus brand of oral semaglutide, which has been on the European market since 2020 and has grown into a multi-billion-dollar franchise. The CHMP recommendation opens a new competitive front between Lilly and Novo Nordisk in Europe’s oral GLP-1 market, adding to their existing rivalry in injectable incretin therapies.What did the clinical evidence show?The weight management recommendation is based on two studies involving more than 4,740 adults with obesity or overweight. The type 2 diabetes recommendation is based on four studies involving 3,765 adults compared against placebo, dapagliflozin, and oral semaglutide.FDA Approves Enspryng for Thyroid Eye DiseaseWhat was approved?The FDA approved Enspryng (satralizumab), an interleukin-6 receptor inhibitor developed by Roche, for adults with thyroid eye disease on October 16. Roche describes it as the first subcutaneous therapy for the condition — one that patients or caregivers can administer at home after training from a healthcare provider. It is Enspryng’s second indication; the drug was first approved in 2020 for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder.What did the clinical trials show?The approval rests on two identically designed Phase 3 trials, SatraGO-1 and SatraGO-2, which enrolled 258 adults across 19 countries. The primary endpoint was the proportion of patients with active, moderate-to-severe disease who achieved at least a 2 mm reduction in proptosis — eye bulging — at week 24. Results diverged: SatraGO-2 met its endpoint, with 52.9% of Enspryng-treated patients achieving a proptosis response versus 23.4% on placebo, and 60.7% showing reduced double vision versus 25.8%. SatraGO-1 did not reach statistical significance, with researchers attributing the gap to an unexpectedly high placebo response.How does this change the treatment landscape?Two disease-specific therapies were already approved — Tepezza and, more recently, Lumvoa — both administered by intravenous infusion. Enspryng’s subcutaneous, every-four-week maintenance dosing offers a different treatment experience, with the key benefit being reduced logistical burden rather than a demonstrated efficacy advantage over existing options. No head-to-head comparison with approved therapies was conducted.What are the remaining unknowns?Roche did not disclose pricing or launch timing. Long-term data beyond week 24 were not described in available sources. Separately, the FDA has granted priority review to a supplemental Enspryng application for myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease, with a decision expected in January 2027. The company was founded in 2018 and reports more than $750 million in capital raised, with existing collaborations with Bristol Myers Squibb, Lilly and Gilead. It has nine programs in development, including genetic regulators of liver fat and fibrosis expected to enter the clinic in early 2027.Why MASH and cardiomyopathies?Both conditions are characterized by disease heterogeneity — a single diagnostic label covering patients whose underlying biology differs — which has complicated treatment development. In MASH, the FDA approved its first treatment, resmetirom (Rezdiffra), in March 2024, but the condition still lacks therapeutic options for most of the estimated 6 to 8 million US patients with moderate-to-advanced liver scarring. The cardiomyopathy scope was not specified in the announcement.What are the limitations of this deal?No drug candidates were named in the announcement. The collaboration sits at the discovery stage, with targets identified through AI-driven analysis still requiring validation through preclinical and clinical work. The $40 million upfront represents less than 3% of the total headline value, and neither company disclosed timelines for milestone payments.FDA Launches Rare Disease Framework InitiativeWhat is the Rare Disease Framework Initiative?The FDA announced a new effort to redesign how drugs and biologics for rare diseases are developed and reviewed. The initiative, outlined in a white paper released by the agency’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, aims to build a regulatory framework tailored to the realities of small patient populations — covering clinical development, evidence standards, manufacturing review, and the role of patient voice throughout the process.Why is FDA doing this now?Despite years of regulatory flexibility programs for rare diseases, only approximately 5% of rare conditions currently have an FDA-approved treatment. The agency says that gap reflects the need for a more fundamentally tailored approach rather than incremental adjustments to a framework originally designed for common diseases.What are the specific commitments?The initiative outlines six priority areas: greater clarity and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance; embedding the patient voice early and at defined milestones; leveraging external expertise for customized review; building shared institutional knowledge; applying risk-based approaches to manufacturing and pre-approval inspections; and championing innovative statistical approaches in rare disease development.What happens next?The FDA is hosting a public meeting on October 28 at its White Oak campus, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to gather input from patients, disease advocates, industry, and other stakeholders. Additional sector-specific roundtables and requests for information will follow. The detailed framework development — which could include new guidance, regulatory changes, and organizational changes within FDA — will be informed by that input.Gilead and Vir Biotechnology Enter $1.87 Billion Masked T-Cell Engager CollaborationWhat are the two companies agreeing to develop?Vir Biotechnology will discover and optimize three novel PRO-XTEN dual-masked T-cell engager development candidates for Gilead, targeting selected solid tumor-associated antigens. Gilead holds an exclusive license to develop, manufacture and commercialize the resulting therapies. Vir will receive $90 million upfront — including $65 million in cash and a $25 million equity investment at a 30% premium — and is eligible for up to $1.74 billion in additional milestones and tiered royalties.What is the PRO-XTEN masking technology?PRO-XTEN is designed to keep T-cell engagers inactive in circulation until they reach the tumor microenvironment, where tumor-specific proteases cleave the mask and activate the drug’s cancer-killing mechanism. That conditional activation is intended to limit systemic toxicity — one of the primary barriers to TCE use in solid tumors — while extending the drug’s half-life and potentially enabling less frequent dosing.Why does this matter for solid tumor oncology?T-cell engagers have proven highly effective in blood cancers but have faced significant limitations in solid tumors, where toxicity and the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment have constrained clinical use. Vir’s PRO-XTEN approach directly targets those barriers. This is the second major PRO-XTEN collaboration — an earlier $1.7 billion deal with Astellas for a PSMA-targeted TCE in prostate cancer was announced in February 2026. Together the two deals bring total PRO-XTEN platform value to more than $3.6 billion across two top-tier pharma partners.How does this fit Gilead’s oncology strategy?Today’s deal is Gilead’s third major solid tumor oncology transaction in 2026, following the $5 billion Tubulis ADC acquisition in April and the $2.1 billion Ouro Medicines BCMA T-cell engager acquisition in March. Gilead is simultaneously building in ADCs, T-cell engagers for autoimmune disease, and now masked T-cell engagers for solid tumors — a deliberate multi-mechanism oncology buildout executed across a single year.Bausch + Lomb Appoints Thomas Appio as Interim CEOWhat happened at Bausch + Lomb?Bausch + Lomb announced that Brent Saunders departed as CEO by mutual agreement, with Thomas J. Appio named interim CEO effective immediately. Appio, who will retain his role as CEO of parent company Bausch Health, steps into the position just weeks before the company reports third-quarter results and updates its full-year guidance on October 28.What does the company expect for 2026?Simultaneously with the leadership announcement, both Bausch + Lomb and Bausch Health said they expect to raise their full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance based on preliminary third-quarter results, citing strong business performance and anticipated momentum through year-end.What was Saunders building?Saunders returned to Bausch + Lomb in March 2023 — his second stint as CEO — and spent three years stabilizing the company’s supply chain, accelerating commercial execution, and rebuilding its R&D pipeline. title: Bristol Myers Squibb Discloses Patient Death in CAR-T Multiple Sclerosis Trial
content: Advertisement News|Articles|October 26, 2026 Bristol Myers Squibb Discloses Patient Death in CAR-T Multiple Sclerosis Trial Author(s)Nicholas Jacobus Bristol Myers Squibb discloses results from it's Phase I Breakfree-2 trial of CAR-T therapy zola-cel for multiple sclerosis. Advertisement Bristol Myers Squibb (BMS) has disclosed a patient death in its early-stage Breakfree-2 trial studying zolacabtagene autoleucel, an investigational, autologous CD19-directed CAR T cell therapy, in patients with relapsing or progressive forms of multiple sclerosis (MS).The death was disclosed as part of a broader data readout presented in an oral presentation at MSToronto 2026 and follows the company’s decision to place a voluntary pause on zola-cel studies back in September.What happened to the patient?The patient, who had highly active relapsing MS, died of septic pneumonia one day after receiving high-dose chemotherapy and 44 days after zola-cel infusion.1 According to BMS, the patient experienced late-onset, non-ICANS motor symptoms following infusion that did not resolve with intermittent corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin.Although the patient’s CAR-T cell expansion was consistent with that observed across the study, physicians administered high-dose cyclophosphamide, after which the patient developed septic pneumonia and died the following day. A BMS spokesperson told Reuters, “The patient had a late onset side effect, a series of other complications and was heavily pretreated prior to CAR T, confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.”2 BMS says the death was unrelated to the earlier voluntary pause and that no additional Grade 5 events have occurred across any zola-cel autoimmune disease program, which has treated 190 patients in Phase I studies to date. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Top of the morning to you. Blue skies, cool breezes, and plenty of chirping birds are enveloping the comfy Pharmalot campus, which is cause to fire up the trusty tea kettle for a needed cuppa stimulation, and we invite you to join us. Remember, a prescription is not required. Our choice today is ginger peach. Meanwhile, here are a few items of interest. Hope you have a smashing day and, of course, do stay in touch. … Over the last year, a few telehealth companies have begun to market off-label prescriptions of GLP-1 drugs, both branded and compounded, to treat alcohol use disorder and other addictions, STAT tells us. Addiction medicine experts see the businesses responding to a significant unmet medical need. As early evidence of the drugs’ promise emerges, and personal stories circulate on social media platforms, some patients have explicitly sought out the drugs to cut down on drinking. Still, telehealth platforms marketing GLP-1s for addiction trouble some experts, who say this could cause fragmented care and potentially inappropriate prescriptions as researchers are still working to understand and vet the unproven treatments.Advertisement The U.S. Department of Treasury is poised to issue a proposed rule as early as tomorrow that would subject outbound U.S. licensing deals with Chinese biotech companies to additional regulatory scrutiny under the COINS Act, Endpoints News reports. The Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act, which was enacted in December 2015, puts some American investment in Chinese technology under Treasury screening. Overall concerns about China’s ambitions and a pervasive anti-pharma view in many parts of Congress and the administration may make it difficult for the pharmaceutical industry to overcome objections, Capital Alpha Partners analyst Rob Smith wrote investors. content: STAT PlusNewsletterPharmalot Pharmalittle: We’re reading about a Roche lung cancer drug, a Bristol CAR-T trial death, and more Most recently approved cancer drugs in Europe do not offer high clinical benefit, analysis finds Manage alerts for this article Save this story for later Share this article Alex Hogan/STAT By Ed SilvermanOct. 26, 2026 Pharmalot Columnist, Senior Writer Ed Silverman[email protected]Ed’s stories explore prescription drug pricing, affordability and access, as well issues surrounding patents, litigation, and legislation. He is also the author of the morning Pharmalittle newsletter and the afternoon Pharmalot newsletter. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to another working week. We hope the weekend respite was relaxing and invigorating because that oh-too-familiar routine of meetings, deadlines, and the like has returned with a vengeance. But what can you do? The world, such as it is, continues to rotate. To nudge it in a better direction, we are brewing another cup of stimulation. Our choice today is butter pecan with a dash of raw honey. Feel free to join us. Remember, no prescription is required. Meanwhile, here are some tidbits to help you along. Best of luck accomplishing your goals today, and of course, do keep in touch. … Bristol Myers Squibb reported that one patient died after receiving its investigational CAR-T therapy in an early autoimmune trial, adding to safety concerns about a growing field of research, STAT notes. In a Phase 1 trial that tested the therapy in multiple sclerosis, the patient experienced motor symptoms that did not resolve with standard autoimmune treatments. They were then given a potent immunosuppressant, but developed septic pneumonia and died, Bristol said in a press release. In a subsequent statement, Bristol said this patient was treated for a series of other complications prior to receiving the CAR-T therapy, “confounding our ability to determine the root cause of the issue.”Advertisement A Roche drug billed as a potential blockbuster helped patients with a form of lung cancer that had spread live almost six months longer than two competitive medicines, Bloomberg News says. The experimental treatment, called divarasib, fared better than similar drugs from Amgen and Bristol Myers Squibb in a late-stage study. The drug was given to patients with non-small cell lung cancer that had spread, in part because of a genetic mutation, after other treatments, including chemotherapy. The findings could help divarasib become the treatment of choice for this type of lung cancer, in which a mutation called KRAS G12C drives the tumor cell growth. In a statement, Caribou CEO Rachel Haurwitz said the current financing environment has made it “increasingly challenging” to secure the money needed to advance the company’s two main research programs, which focus on a hard-to-make form of medicine known as “off-the-shelf” cell therapy. As such, Caribou has made the “difficult decision” not to further develop its programs and to “evaluate strategic alternatives” — common corporate lingo for opening itself up to various deals. Caribou’s board of directors has already cleared management to start evaluating a potential merger, acquisition, business combination or other transactions. The company has also tapped Wedbush Securities to serve as its exclusive financial advisor in this process. To Daina Graybosch, an analyst at Leerink Partners who covers Caribou, the natural end for the company now is either a reverse merger or an acquisition by Tang Capital, a San Diego-based investment firm that made a name for itself by buying up cash-rich biotechs and returning much of their value to shareholders. Caribou ended the second quarter with $114 million worth of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. “I think Rachel and the team really do believe in their assets, but it's a real struggle,” Graybosch said. “And when you finally do raise [capital], it just gets more and more dilutive. To pull the trigger now and give money back is what everybody likes to see” and “creates so much positive trust” with investors. if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { googletag.cmd.push(function() { googletag.defineSlot( '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2', [[300, 250], 'fluid'], 'dfp-hybrid2-mobile' ).addService(googletag.pubads()); }); } waitToLoadAds.push(function() { googletag.cmd.push(function() { if (window.dfp_visibility === 'mobile' ) { window.onDvtagReady?.(() => googletag.display('dfp-hybrid2-mobile')); googletag.pubads().addEventListener('slotRenderEnded', function (event) { var adUnitPath = '/3618/biopharmadive/biopharmadivehybrid2'; var onProformative = false; if (onProformative && event.slot.getAdUnitPath() === adUnitPath && !event.isEmpty ) { var adUnitPathWithVisibility = adUnitPath + '-mobile'; var selector = '.pf-comments__ad-wrapper #dfp-hybrid2-mobile'; if (!$(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').hasClass('borders')) { $(selector).closest('.pf-comments__ad-wrapper').addClass('borders') } } }); } }); }); Caribou checks some of the boxes that, according to deal experts, make for a good reverse merger candidate. It trades on the Nasdaq, for example, which is more attractive to private drug developers than lower-tier, over-the-counter markets. A researcher works in Caribou's labs, where the company was designing cell therapies for blood malignancies. Permission granted by Caribou Biosciences Caribou may also have a subzero enterprise value, which, in broad strokes, means that after accounting for its cash pile, the market is attributing nothing — or, really, less than nothing — to the company’s core operating business. That can actually be a plus to private developers, as it signals they might not have to pay a big premium to snag the public vehicle. Using its June 30 financials and closing share price Wednesday, Caribou would have a negative enterprise value of roughly $20 million. (Notably, that’s at the low end of a range from Leerink, which estimates the figure could be as much as $30 million depending on how much cash Caribou spent in the third quarter.) “I would definitely say a reverse merger is on the table here,” said Emmett Sweeney, a vice president on the healthcare investment banking team at Raymond James. Perhaps what makes Caribou such an obvious reverse merger prospect is it publicly stating that it’s exploring strategic alternatives. When companies do that, they become “low-hanging fruit” for reverse merger deals, according to David Kellman, a managing director and head of life sciences and biopharma investment banking at Citizens. They’re “basically running auction processes” with private companies, Kellman said in an interview earlier this month. “Those are the most obvious candidates, regardless of other criteria.” Caribou’s statement, including the mention of Wedbush being its strategic advisor, is a sign that company leaders are “serious” and “mean business,” Sweeney said. Clearly, “they want to move quickly. That's another aspect of Caribou that makes it an attractive merger partner.” Sweeney and others anticipate that Caribou, if not already, will soon be inundated with inbounds from private companies interested in merging. With roughly two dozen biotech reverse mergers announced this year, “the question for many companies is no longer whether the structure works, but whether they can find the right shell and execute the transaction on attractive terms,” Raymond James analysts wrote in a note to clients Wednesday. One lingering question is whether Caribou’s now-discontinued drugs will find a new home. Graybosch doesn’t have high hopes — in part because of rival programs advancing at other cell therapy developers like Fate Therapeutics and AvenCell Therapeutics, both of which are backed by major life sciences investors and large pharmaceutical firms. “Very rarely do these assets show up [again],” she said. “If I'm an investor thinking, ‘Do I wrap a new company around this asset, or do I go invest in AvenCell or Fate,’ I probably choose AvenCell or Fate at this point.” Recommended Reading A booming business on Wall Street would love more biotechs to quietly die By Jacob Bell • Sept. 10, 2026 Add us on Google Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Filed Under: Deals

title: Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal
content: An article from Dive Brief // Obesity drugs Corxel, an obesity drugmaker, to go public via SPAC deal Armed with a $300 million financing and two GLP-1 and amylin-targeting medicines, Corxel is set to become the latest weight loss-focused company to join the public markets. Published Oct. 26, 2026 Gwendolyn Wu Senior Reporter Share Copy link Email LinkedIn X/Twitter Facebook Print License Add us on Google Corxel U.S. will go public via a merger with the SPAC Amanat Acquisition Corp., the companies announced Oct. 26, 2026. Michael Santiago/Getty Images via Getty Images Dive Brief: Corxel Pharmaceuticals, a drug startup developing a pair of weight loss medicines, announced Monday plans to go public by merging with a special purpose acquisition company. The SPAC deal and concurrent $300 million private investment will help Corxel take CX11, a GLP-1 pill licensed from the Chinese drug developer Vincentage Pharma, into late-stage testing. In June, Corxel said CX11 helped participants in a U.S. Phase 2 trial lose an average of up to 11.5% of their body weight after 36 weeks while displaying a “favorable” gastrointestinal tolerability profile. The combined company will also advance a preclinical weight loss prospect directed at a different gut hormone known as amylin. A third drug licensed from Biogen and in development for acute ischemic stroke isn't part of the deal and will instead be housed in a parent entity. Corxel's backers made clear in subsequent talks that they wanted the company to have a "more dedicated focus," rather than pursue "two different tracks," said Kevin Xie, its chief financial officer, in an interview with BioPharma Dive. What followed was a split, with two obesity drugs being merged into a publicly traded entity and the rest of Corxel funneled into a still-private parent. “Both companies have separate development strategies and financing processes, so that’s more welcome news to the investors,” Xie said. Formerly known as Ji Xing Pharmaceuticals, Corxel launched in 2019 and once planned to develop a nasal spray for dry eye disease. It offloaded that therapy in 2024, the same year it acquired from Biogen most rights to JX10 and licensed CX11 from Vincentage. CX11 was already in human testing when Corxel struck that deal. Now it’s on the verge of a global late-stage study. Corxel reported positive late-stage data in May from a Chinese trial run by Vincentage. An international Phase 3 test could follow as soon as the first quarter of 2027. Corxel is pitching CX11 as a “differentiated, next-generation” therapy and an option for people who don’t stay on injectable GLP-1s. Though it is well behind first-to-market oral GLP-1s like Eli Lilly’s Foundayo and Novo’s Wegovy pill, Xie said CX11 may be appealing to people who need to lose 5% to 10% of their body weight and are classified as overweight, but not obese. (Around 31% of U.S. adults fit this description, according to one National Institutes of Health estimate.) Corxel is testing higher doses of CX11 in a Phase 1b trial in an effort to explore the drug’s “efficacy upside,” according to a statement. Additional data are expected in the first half of 2027.
